description: From the pn junction to power stages: how diodes, transistors and operational amplifiers shape continuous signals. Students build, bias, measure and break amplifiers, filters and oscillators on the circuit bench and check them against hand calculations and Arduino measurements.
modelledOn: Horowitz and Hill, The Art of Electronics
outcomes: Explain the operation of diodes, bipolar and MOS transistors from their device physics and I-V characteristics.
Bias a transistor stage at a stable operating point and derive its small-signal gain and impedances.
Design operational-amplifier circuits for summing, filtering, instrumentation and signal conditioning.
Predict amplifier frequency response and analyse the effect of negative feedback on gain, bandwidth and stability.
Design active filters, oscillators and linear power stages to a specification, and verify them by measurement.

units.title: Semiconductors and diodes
topics: Intrinsic and doped silicon: electrons, holes, drift and diffusion currents
The pn junction: depletion region, built-in potential, forward and reverse bias
The Shockley diode equation, temperature dependence and the diode load line
Rectifiers: half-wave, full-wave and bridge circuits; smoothing capacitor and ripple voltage
Zener regulators, clippers, clampers, LEDs and photodiodes

units.title: Bipolar and MOS transistors
topics: BJT structure and the cutoff, active and saturation regions
BJT characteristics: common-emitter curves, current gain beta, Early effect
The BJT as a switch: driving an LED or relay from a logic pin
MOSFET structure: enhancement mode, threshold voltage, channel formation
MOSFET characteristics: triode and saturation regions, square-law model, channel-length modulation
The MOSFET as a switch and the CMOS inverter transfer curve

units.title: Biasing and small-signal models
topics: BJT bias circuits: fixed bias, emitter feedback and voltage-divider bias; stability factor
MOSFET bias circuits: gate divider, source degeneration, current-source bias
The Q-point, DC load line and thermal runaway
Small-signal models: hybrid-pi and T-models for BJT; gm, r-pi and ro for BJT and MOSFET
AC equivalent circuits, coupling and bypass capacitors

units.title: Single-stage and multi-stage amplifiers
topics: Common-emitter and common-source amplifiers: voltage gain, input and output resistance
Emitter and source followers as buffers
Common-base, common-gate and the cascode configuration
Cascaded stages: loading effects, overall gain and Darlington pairs
The differential pair: differential and common-mode gain, CMRR
Current mirrors and active loads

units.title: Operational amplifier circuits
topics: The ideal op amp, virtual short and the two golden rules
Inverting, non-inverting, summing and difference amplifiers
Integrators and differentiators; practical compensation resistors
The instrumentation amplifier and sensor interfacing: thermistor, strain gauge, load cell
Comparators, hysteresis and the Schmitt trigger
Non-ideal behaviour: input offset, bias current, slew rate, gain-bandwidth product

units.title: Frequency response and feedback
topics: Decibels, poles, zeros and Bode plots of magnitude and phase
Low-frequency and high-frequency response of transistor amplifiers; Miller effect
Gain-bandwidth trade-off and rise time versus bandwidth
Negative feedback: four topologies and effects on gain, bandwidth, impedance and distortion
Stability: loop gain, gain margin, phase margin and frequency compensation

units.title: Filters and oscillators
topics: Active low-pass and high-pass filters: Sallen-Key and Butterworth responses
Band-pass and notch filters; filter Q and cascade design
Barkhausen criterion; RC phase-shift and Wien-bridge oscillators
LC oscillators (Colpitts, Hartley) and crystal oscillators
The 555 timer in astable and monostable mode; relaxation oscillators

units.title: Power stages and regulators
topics: Class A, B and AB output stages: efficiency and crossover distortion
Power dissipation, thermal resistance and heat-sink sizing
Linear regulators: series pass transistor, 78xx and low-dropout devices
Switching regulators: buck and boost converters and efficiency
Power supply design for an unreliable grid: battery, solar charging and brown-out protection

schedule.title: Semiconductors and the pn junction
schedule.exercise: Explain in a half page how doping creates n-type and p-type silicon, then compute the diode current for a 0.65 V forward bias at 300 K given the saturation current.

tasks.title: Sweep a silicon diode from 0 to 1 V in the circuit bench and plot current against voltage to find the turn-on voltage
Plot the Shockley diode equation for three saturation currents and temperatures, and describe how the knee voltage shifts with each
Solve a diode and resistor circuit with the load line graphically, then compare the operating point with the bench measurement and with the constant-drop model

schedule.title: Rectifiers, regulators and special diodes
schedule.exercise: Size the smoothing capacitor for a bridge rectifier delivering 12 V at 200 mA with at most 1 V ripple from the 50 Hz Ghana mains, and design a 5.1 V Zener regulator for a sensor board.

tasks.title: Build a half-wave rectifier with a 10 V peak sine source and record the output waveform with and without a smoothing capacitor
Build a Zener shunt regulator and plot output voltage as the load current rises from 0 to 40 mA to find where regulation fails
Design a bridge rectifier and filter for 9 V at 300 mA with under 5 percent ripple, then measure ripple and compare it with your formula

schedule.title: Bipolar junction transistor operation
schedule.exercise: From a given set of measured IC-VCE curves, extract beta and the Early voltage, mark the regions on the plot, and size the base resistor so a BJT switches a 100 mA relay fully on.

tasks.title: Set the base current of an npn transistor to three values and record which region the transistor is in for each collector supply
Sweep VCE at five base currents to draw the IC-VCE family of curves and estimate beta and the Early voltage
Fit a straight line to the active-region data for three transistors, compute their Early voltages, and explain which would give the highest voltage gain

schedule.title: MOSFETs and transistor switching
schedule.exercise: Compute the drain current of an n-channel MOSFET in triode and saturation for given VGS and VDS, and size the gate resistor and pull-down for a MOSFET that switches a 2 A load from a 3.3 V logic pin.

tasks.title: Wire an n-channel MOSFET to an Arduino pin to switch a 12 V LED strip, and record the gate voltage at which it turns fully on
Sweep VGS on an n-channel MOSFET to plot the transfer curve, mark the threshold voltage and check the square-law fit
Build a CMOS inverter, sweep its input from 0 to 5 V, and read off the switching threshold and noise margins from the transfer curve

schedule.title: Biasing and small-signal models
schedule.exercise: Design a voltage-divider bias for a BJT with ICQ of 1 mA from a 12 V supply, compute gm and r-pi from the result, and show how the Q-point moves when beta doubles.

tasks.title: Build a voltage-divider biased common-emitter stage and measure the quiescent collector current and VCE against the hand calculation
Replace the transistor with beta 100, then 200, then 300, and compare how much the Q-point moves for fixed bias and for divider bias
Compute gm, r-pi and ro for a transistor at five bias currents and plot each against collector current on log axes

schedule.title: Single-stage amplifiers
schedule.exercise: For a common-emitter amplifier with given bias values, derive voltage gain, input resistance and output resistance, then compare with a source follower on the same transistor.

tasks.title: Drive a common-emitter amplifier with a 10 mV sine at 1 kHz and measure the voltage gain and the phase inversion
Add an emitter follower after a high-resistance source and show by measurement how much loading it removes
Build a cascode amplifier, measure its gain and output resistance, and compare both with a single common-emitter stage at the same bias

schedule.title: Multistage amplifiers, differential pairs and mirrors
schedule.exercise: Cascade two common-emitter stages, compute the overall gain including the loading of the second stage on the first, and explain why the product of unloaded gains overestimates it.

tasks.title: Build a two-transistor current mirror and verify that the output current follows a 1 mA reference across four load resistors
Cascade two common-emitter stages with a coupling capacitor, measure total gain and compare it with the product of the individual gains
Build a differential pair with a current-source tail, measure differential gain and common-mode gain, and compute the CMRR in decibels

schedule.title: Op-amp fundamentals and linear circuits
schedule.exercise: Derive the gain of the inverting and non-inverting amplifiers from the golden rules and design a summing amplifier that mixes three audio inputs with gains of 1, 2 and 4.

tasks.title: Build an inverting amplifier of gain -10 and a non-inverting amplifier of gain 11, and verify both with a 100 mV sine input
Build a three-input summing amplifier with weights 1, 2 and 4 and test it with eight combinations of DC inputs against the formula
Build an integrator with a reset resistor, feed a square wave, and explain the drift you see before and after adding the resistor

schedule.title: Op-amp interfacing and limitations
schedule.exercise: Design a thermistor interface that maps 20 to 50 degrees Celsius onto 0 to 5 V, then list which op-amp limits (offset, slew rate, bandwidth) would first spoil its accuracy.

tasks.title: Build an op-amp comparator with a 2.5 V reference and show the output switching as a ramp input crosses the threshold
Connect a thermistor through a conditioning amplifier to an Arduino analogue pin, calibrate with two known temperatures, and log readings
Drive a unity-gain follower with a fast square wave, measure the slew rate, and find the highest sine frequency at 5 V peak without distortion

schedule.title: Frequency response of amplifiers
schedule.exercise: Sketch the Bode magnitude plot for a transfer function with one zero and two poles, then find the 3 dB bandwidth of a common-emitter stage given its capacitances and Miller multiplier.

tasks.title: Plot the Bode magnitude and phase of a first-order RC low-pass filter and mark the corner frequency and the -20 dB per decade slope
Run an AC sweep from 10 Hz to 10 MHz on a common-emitter amplifier and read off the lower and upper 3 dB frequencies
Increase the collector resistor to raise the gain, re-run the sweep, and show that the gain times bandwidth product stays roughly constant

schedule.title: Feedback and stability
schedule.exercise: Show with loop-gain algebra how series-shunt feedback with gain 100 on an amplifier with open-loop gain 10,000 stabilises gain and widens bandwidth, and compute the phase margin from a Bode plot.

tasks.title: Add a feedback resistor to an op-amp stage and measure closed-loop gain, comparing the result with the 1/beta prediction
Apply negative feedback to a transistor amplifier and measure the change in gain, bandwidth and distortion for a 1 kHz sine input
Plot loop gain magnitude and phase for a three-pole amplifier, extract the phase margin, and choose a compensation capacitor that gives 60 degrees

schedule.title: Active filters and oscillators
schedule.exercise: Design a second-order Butterworth low-pass filter with a 3 kHz corner for a voice line, and select component values for a Wien-bridge oscillator at 1 kHz.

tasks.title: Build a 555 astable circuit for a 1 Hz LED flasher and verify frequency and duty cycle on the timing view
Build a Sallen-Key low-pass filter with a 3 kHz corner, run an AC sweep, and check the corner frequency and roll-off
Build a Wien-bridge oscillator at 1 kHz, tune the gain until oscillation starts and holds without clipping, and report the amplitude and distortion

schedule.title: Power stages, thermal design and regulators
schedule.exercise: Compute efficiency and dissipation of a class AB stage delivering 5 W into 8 ohms, select a heat sink for a 7805 dropping 12 V to 5 V at 500 mA, and compare with a buck converter.

tasks.title: Build a linear regulator with a pass transistor and Zener reference, and measure line and load regulation across 9 to 15 V input
Build a class B push-pull stage, view the crossover distortion on a sine input, then remove it with a small bias to class AB
Compare a linear regulator and a buck converter feeding a 5 V sensor load from a 12 V battery, and compute the battery runtime for each
